Kursenai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiaulių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Kursenai's Jewish community, settled in the second half of the 18th century, reached 48 percent of the population by 1897, though significant emigration to South Africa and America had already begun even before WWI further devastated the town. By 1931, 91 percent of local businesses were Jewish-owned, and the community's artisans organized their own union alongside a charitable loan fund that offered adult education courses in Lithuanian language and arithmetic. Two new prayer houses were built in 1921 to replace a synagogue destroyed during WWI. When Germany invaded in June 1941, only about 30 families managed to escape via Latvia; Jewish men were shot in a nearby forest that July, and women and children were deported to Žagarė and murdered there with that town's own Jewish community in August. Only one man and one woman, sheltered by Lithuanian peasants, survived. This cemetery was established in 1752, the same year the first Jews settled and received permission to bury their dead; after the community's total destruction, it was abandoned, and almost no gravestones survive today — likely repurposed as building material, leaving only seven visible stone fragments.
